thread:
alex: heads-up — since the new allocator winback landed i've been seeing route flip-flops between us-east and eu-west for a handful of tenants. hedged requests spike and p99 latency oscillates.
jin: ugh. repro logs?
alex: pasted snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z route=us-east chosen_score=0.72
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z probe eu-west ok -> weight bump -> chosen_score eu-west=0.74
2026-03-15T14:02:14Z commit route=eu-west preempt=soft
2026-03-15T14:02:16Z probe us-east ok -> winback -> chosen_score us-east=0.76
2026-03-15T14:02:16Z commit route=us-east preempt=soft
```
sara: looks like winback increments are identical to probe increments, so small signal noise bounces the selection.
ben: is this just a small tenant profile or broad?
alex: started with high-Q tenants (lots of short chats) but now it's visible across a cost-sensitive shard.
jin: is hedging TTL interacting? if hedged requests target both routes we might be amplifying.
shiv (product): customer reports brief quality regressions when model falls back during the flip. they're hitting retries and seeing duplicated tokens. not great.
ben: two options off the cuff: 1) add hysteresis to winback (e.g., require sustained probe success N seconds) 2) scale down incremental ramp and use a probabilistic backoff.
sara: also consider decoupling probe weight scale from winback weight — probes inform health, winback should be throttled by a separate ramp controller.
allocator-bot: /metric spike alert tenants=13 region-flip-rate=0.18 per_min threshold=0.05
jin: i sketched a tiny change in the allocator: keep a "candidate_score" and require delta > delta_threshold AND consecutive_successes >= K before applying full weight. otherwise apply a fractional alpha multiply.
alex: that seems safe. can you paste the pseudo?
jin: sure: 
```pseudo
on-critical: delta = new_probe_score - current_score
if delta > DELTA && consecutive_ok >= K:
  current_score += min(delta, MAX_RAMP)
else:
  current_score += delta * SLOW_ALPHA
```
alex: nit: we should clamp MAX_RAMP relative to tenant volatility history. don't want a one-size rule.
sara: agree — keep tenant-specific volatility window (EWMA) and use it to shrink MAX_RAMP, maybe also increase K for high-volatility tenants.
shiv (product): timeline? customers need a short-term mitigation. can we feature-flag a conservative winback mode?
ben: yes. we can ship a flag that flips to conservative alpha=0.1 and K=3. no schema change in policy DSL, runtime-only.
jin: i'll prototype and run gated sim against replay traces. can someone run a quick sim job with last 48h traces? alex?
alex: on it — kicking off replay now.
allocator-bot: replay job started job_id=rp-20260315-99
alex: initial run shows flip-rate down 7x with alpha=0.12 and K=3, p99 latency stabilized. small throughput drop ~0.6%.
shiv (product): OK ship the feature flag as mitigation, then follow up w/ RFC for a longer-term change that adds tenant-volatility controls to ramp.
sara: for RFC i'd like to discuss: (a) metricized SLO for flip-rate, (b) API to surface tenant EWMA volatility to policy, (c) policy-level knob for per-tenant ramp/clamp.
jin: also add integration test: simulate probes with correlated noise to catch oscillations in CI.
ben: Ops note — make sure rollout plan includes dedicated logs so we can revert quickly by tenant if token duplication resurfaces.
alex: sounds good. action items: jin prototype + sim (ETA 2d), alex run expanded replay (ETA 1d), bem/ops add feature-flag rollout playbook, sara draft RFC (target next Wed).
shiv (product): i'll loop in support for customer comms once we have the feature flag change.
alex: thanks all. will post results of replay job here.
